findings.finding: The backfill logic at process_snapshot line 697 calls `_file_impact_scope({}, state.get('file_impact') or [])` with an empty dict as the first arg. The _file_impact_scope function at line 531 checks `if data.get('file_impact_scope') == 'none'`, which will always be false when called with `{}`. This is correct for the pre-feature backfill (the old snapshot won't have file_impact_scope set), but the implementation assumes _file_impact_scope is designed to work with both event.data dicts (which may carry the new fields) and empty dicts (which never do). The contract is implicit and not documented.
findings.location: src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:697 (backfill call to _file_impact_scope)
scenarios: A future developer modifies _file_impact_scope and assumes data is always event.data, breaking the backfill path

findings.suggested_fix: Add a docstring to _file_impact_scope explaining the dual use: 'Derive the tri-state declaration from event.data (which may carry the new fields) or from empty dict during SNAPSHOT backfill (line 697). When called from backfill with {}, the tri-state is derived purely from the paths array; when called from process_file_impact with real event.data, the new fields are respected if present.'
